Even when Asian money is flowing overseas, Treasuries aren’t necessarily the default first choice.

Korean investors prefer stocks, while Taiwan’s money has shifted towards equities and deposits, according to Brad Setser, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations and a former US Treasury official. “So some friends with big surpluses haven’t been big net buyers,” he said.

Setser sees this as part of a broader “dereservification” trend, in which more foreign assets are held outside traditional central-bank reserves and instead flow through pension funds, state banks and other large institutions. That doesn’t amount to de-dollarisation, but can mean less “official demand” for Treasuries, according to Setser.

"Elevated dollar funding rates continue to erode returns on Treasuries just as rising domestic yields have improved opportunities in JGBs," says Andre de Silva, Markets Live strategist at Bloomberg Strategists.

Higher yields elsewhere are also giving investors options. Korea’s Kiwoom Asset Management remains cautious on Treasuries and sees Japanese government bonds as relatively attractive, said Yang Joo Kyung, head of global fixed income.

Japanese investors have more reason to keep their money at home too. With domestic yields at multi-decade highs, the extra return they can earn from investing overseas has narrowed.

“Japan is a US ally, and we’ve certainly seen some signs that there is a kind of gradual unwind of the carry trade,” said Oliver Levingston, G10 foreign-exchange and rates strategist at BofA Securities, referring to the practice of borrowing cheaply in yen to invest in higher-yielding assets elsewhere.

That doesn’t mean the US is running out of buyers. Private investors, including hedge funds, banks and mutual funds, have stepped in, boosting their share of federal debt to about 70%, near the highest since 1990.

But they’re more sensitive to price. For Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh, that means markets can react sharply if investors grow uneasy about monetary policy, the economy, widening US deficits or signals coming from the White House.

That sensitivity contributed to benchmark 10-year yields rising above 5% this year. They climbed about three basis points to 5.02% on Wednesday.

The countries least aligned with Washington bought US$17.1 billion of Treasuries from January through August, reversing four straight years of selling over the same period. That’s a tenth of what US-aligned countries bought.

China remains the biggest seller, ahead of Korea, though some analysts believe Beijing might have channeled some transactions through other nations, including Canada. Belgium — whose holdings are thought to include some Chinese accounts — ranked third. The UK, Hong Kong and India were the biggest buyers.

“China’s continued reductions are consistent with a longer-term diversification trend, even as the underlying motivations are harder to establish,” said Laura Cooper, London-based head of macro credit at Nuveen.

This isn’t the first time US-aligned countries have pulled back from Treasuries. They sold sharply in 2020, when the Covid-19 pandemic triggered a global scramble for liquidity.

Even so, the US$32 trillion Treasury market remains unmatched in its depth, liquidity and near round-the-clock trading, while the dollar retains its role as the world’s dominant reserve currency.

Foreigners still owned US$7.85 trillion of Treasuries as of August, near an all-time high, though their share of the market has shrunk to less than a third from a peak of 52% in 2012.

“When you look at the alternatives, they’re pretty few and far between,” said Robert Tipp, head of global bonds at PGIM. “So you have had a rebalancing and consistent runoff from some countries, but it’s been absorbed by others.”

Foreign investors aren’t abandoning US assets either. Some of that money is shifting into American equities and corporate debt, suggesting investors remain keen on US companies even as appetite for government debt cools.

And the buyers filling the gap are likely to demand more compensation than the friendly nations that used to fund Washington with little fuss.

“The Treasury will fund itself — the question is the price and the volatility of the price,” said Shoki Omori, Deutsche Bank AG’s chief fixed-income strategist for Japan. “What the level cannot buy back is the patient, price-insensitive money the allies used to supply.”

title: Danone sales rise on higher prices, medical nutrition demand
article:
(Oct 28): Danone SA sales climbed in the third quarter, driven by higher prices and persistent demand for its protein-rich yoghurts and fortified drinks for the elderly and ill.

Like-for-like sales rose 4%, the producer of Oikos Greek yoghurt said in a statement Wednesday, above the 3.7% estimate of analysts in a Bloomberg survey. Increased pricing added 3.6% to sales growth — a bigger share than expected — while volume growth lagged.

The specialised nutrition unit showed the strongest jump in sales, topping estimates on strength in Asia and the Americas. A poor performance linked to adverse weather hit the Mizone waters business in Asia, shaving a percentage point off group sales growth in the quarter.

The results are “a mixed bag", Jefferies analysts led by David Hayes said in a note.

The shares rose as much as 2.7% in early Paris trading. The stock was down 20% this year through Tuesday’s close, trailing rival Nestle SA and on course for the worst annual performance since 2020.

CEO Antoine de Saint-Affrique has led a turnaround in five years atop the company by shedding weaker businesses and expanding in areas like high-protein dairy offerings and food for cancer patients. The rise of weight-loss drugs has spurred demand for protein-rich, gut-friendly products.

See also: What to know about plague after suspected Russia lab worker case

Still, weakness in the US has weighed on sentiment. Danone announced a host of changes to boost performance in the US “with a sense of urgency", deputy CEO Juergen Esser told investors Wednesday. “We are obviously not satisfied with this performance in light of a market which is growing faster.”

Danone has added production capacity of high-protein yoghurts at four of its US factories and will continue to add more. “Capacity is at the end of Q3 no longer a limiting factor to our growth,” Esser said.

Another change is new leadership, bringing Francois Lacombe from Danone’s Spanish business across to the US. Danone next year will also launch kefir, fibre-enriched products and a new natural Greek yoghurt to add to its existing “performance” Greek yoghurt brand, Oikos.

See also: PRECISE and AWS to build systems for Singapore’s 450,000-person genomics study

Danone confirmed its guidance to increase like-for-like sales between 3% and 5% this year, with recurring operating income growing faster than sales.

Earlier this year, Danone agreed to buy UK-based Huel, a maker of fortified protein powders and ready-to-consume drinks and meals popular with gym-goers. It also acquired Australian dairy company Made Group to expand its offerings of coconut water and protein shakes in Asia.

title: Thailand holds key rate, lifts growth outlook on AI exports
article:
(Oct 28): Thailand’s central bank held its benchmark interest rate and boosted economic growth forecasts for the second time this year as the artificial intelligence boom drives exports.

The seven-member Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously on Wednesday to keep the one-day repurchase rate at 1%, its lowest level since September 2022. The decision was expected by all 23 economists surveyed by Bloomberg.

The fourth-straight hold extends the longest run of unchanged decisions in two years and was in line with earlier signals from policymakers. Inflation has remained manageable enough to allow the central bank to maintain an accommodative policy stance while the government works to support an economy hurt by higher energy costs.

While describing the economy as continuing to grow below potential, the central bank upgraded its economic growth forecast to 2.4% this year and 2.1% in 2027, from earlier projections of 2.3% and 1.8%. The BOT sees tamer price pressures, with core inflation seen averaging 1.2% and 1.3% this year and next, down from June’s estimates of 1.5% and 1.4%.

“The committee believes that the current interest rate is appropriate to support economic recovery,” the central bank said. “While inflation is projected to rise temporarily due to supply-side factors, the committee will need to monitor inflation trends and risks, as well as the long-term impact of low interest rates on economic and financial stability.”

The BOT said growth has been driven by better-than-expected exports and investment in light of global demand for AI, but that other sectors of the economy are still facing constraints.

See also: StanChart beats estimates, raises targets on wealth boom

The number of foreign tourist arrivals is expected to decline amid higher oil prices, it said. Private consumption continues to be limited by elevated household debt, fragile labour market conditions and weak purchasing power, particularly among low-income households facing cost-of-living pressure, the BOT said.

The Thai baht narrowed losses to 0.1% against the US dollar after the decision while the benchmark stock index was down 0.3%.

The BOT said that the baht has been dragged lower this year by the prospect of tighter US monetary policy, along with rising oil prices, while Thai government bond yields are edging higher due to the global selloff in fixed-income markets.

See also: South Korea's financial firms hit by more hacks as Asia breaches grow

Most economists surveyed before the decision expected Thailand’s benchmark rate to remain at 1% through the end of 2027, though JPMorgan Chase & Co, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and Bank of America Corp have highlighted a growing likelihood of tightening next year.

The Southeast Asian economy has shown signs of improvement, with exports rising 24% from a year earlier in September as the AI boom lifted demand for electronics. Imports surged 50.4%, driven by fuel and capital goods. The government may also revise this year’s gross domestic product growth figures following an overhaul of the manufacturing production index to better capture new industries.

Thailand’s decision adds to a mixed regional policy picture. The Philippines delivered a surprise 50-basis-point hike last week to fight inflation while Indonesia and Singapore have recently kept policy settings unchanged.

title: Saudi tanker giant posts 10-fold profit jump as ship rates surge
article:
(Oct 28): Saudi Arabia’s main shipping firm Bahri reported a 10-fold jump in third-quarter profit as its oil tanker business benefited from surging freight rates amid the Iran war.

Net income rose to 5.1 billion riyals from 513 million riyals a year earlier, the company said Wednesday in a stock exchange statement. Sales at its oil unit increased by roughly 10 times due to higher rates and chartering levels.

The US and Israeli attacks on Iran at the end of February sparked a regional war that led to the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint at the mouth of the Persian Gulf. In recent months, attacks on tankers transiting the crucial waterway have failed to stem a rising flow of oil out of the Gulf.

Several Bahri vessels were attacked during the period and two of the company’s mariners were killed in the incidents, CEO Ahmed Al Subaey said in the statement. The regional war has contributed to “an exceptionally complex operating environment", he said.

Bahri, officially called the National Shipping Company of Saudi Arabia, has been instrumental in helping state oil producer Aramco to ramp up crude exports via Hormuz. Aramco has looked to regain market share by supplying mainly Chinese buyers with oil via ship-to-ship transfer outside Hormuz, after its East-West pipeline was attacked and temporarily put out of service in September.

Overall Gulf oil exports have recovered to near pre-war levels as more regional producers send barrels through Hormuz, relying in part on convoys with military protection and sailing with location signals switched off to avoid detection.

See also: This oil tanker tycoon's WhatsApp messages drive big market moves

title: Weaker euro boosts European exporters as earnings season peaks
article:
(Oct 28): The dollar’s rebound is good news for shares in European exporters, just as companies enter the busiest stretch of the third-quarter reporting season.

The euro has fallen more than 5% against the greenback this year and roughly 2% in the past month alone, a boon for firms that sell to customers outside Europe. It is a reversal of the headwind that held back profits for these stocks earlier in 2026, and some strategists say it has yet to be fully factored in by the market.

A UBS Group AG basket of stocks exposed to US sales, including the likes of Novo Nordisk A/S, Diageo plc, GSK plc and Rentokil Initial plc, has rallied almost 8% this month, the most since July 2022.

Companies representing nearly 40% of the Stoxx 600’s market capitalisation are reporting this week and next. A weaker euro is a handy boost for an index whose members generate roughly half their revenue overseas.

Strategists at HSBC Holdings plc estimate that a 5% depreciation in European currencies against the dollar can add about 3.1 percentage points to regional earnings growth. But even a relatively small currency impact can make a difference in a market buffeted by negative news.

See also: Marcos pledges to ‘do all we can’ to defend Philippine peso

With sentiment on edge, investors are looking to earnings for signs of stability, according to Michael Field, Morningstar’s head of European equity strategy.

A weaker euro may help by “turning some meets into beats,” Field said. “There is an awareness of how much it’s bringing to the table, but I still don’t think it’s fully in the price.”

The benefit may be greatest where earnings expectations are subdued. Field cited consumer companies, including Unilever plc and Nestlé SA, where weaker demand and higher costs have weighed on the outlook. “That extra bump from FX could actually make a huge difference,” he said.

See also: Singapore dollar gains on yen as carry funder, analysts say

European healthcare is another potential beneficiary, generating roughly 40% of its revenue in the US, the highest among Stoxx 600 sectors. Oddo BHF estimates the recent dollar move could add 2.5%-3.5% to Novo Nordisk’s earnings per share and 2%-3% at Sanofi SA. Both report within the next two weeks.

Currency effects also mean fund managers can find stock opportunities in countries where broader economic conditions look less appealing.

“I may have a cautious view of the UK and European economies over the next few years,” said Dan Hanbury, a global equity portfolio manager at Ninety One. “However, that is very different from being cautious on their stock markets given how much of the revenue is made overseas.”

For all that, what benefits Europe’s international earners isn’t necessarily good for the market as a whole.

European equities have historically tended to outperform other regions when the euro strengthens, according to Jitania Kandhari, deputy chief investment officer at Morgan Stanley Investment Management. That partly reflects the region’s large weighting toward domestically exposed financials, which benefit from the stronger purchasing power, economic activity and credit growth associated with a stronger euro.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

“You really need euro strength for the aggregate MSCI Europe to outperform on a relative basis,” Kandhari said. A sustained decline would make her more cautious on parts of southern Europe, where domestic financials carry significant weight.

At the individual-stock level, the picture gets more complicated still. Adidas AG and Puma SE have dollar-denominated Asian sourcing, meaning sustained greenback strength can ultimately hurt margins, while sophisticated hedging can delay or mute the benefit for exporters.

Hanbury points to Rolls-Royce Holdings plc, among his firm’s top picks, where a large hedge book covers multi-year airline servicing contracts.

“The problem is timing and hedging, and it’s never as exact as you’d like it to be,” Hanbury said. “Hedging creates a lag in the numbers coming through.”

For longer-term investors, that complexity makes currency another risk to manage rather than the basis for an investment thesis. Rathbones fund manager David Coombs said he is willing to tolerate short-term foreign-exchange volatility in globally diversified businesses such as L’Oreal SA but becomes more cautious when several holdings leave a portfolio exposed to the same currency.

“The currency is the last decision in the chain,” Coombs said, adding that it’s difficult to forecast its impact on overall profits and returns.

The euro’s continued weakness potentially sets up a further earnings boost. Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman, sees scope for the currency to weaken toward US$1.10 by year-end as US economic outperformance and interest-rate differentials continue to favour the dollar.

The reason behind any further weakness still matters. A euro falling because of strong US growth has different implications for European assets than a decline caused by investors demanding a higher risk premium at home.

French fiscal stress can boost exporters’ translated earnings through a weaker currency while simultaneously pushing up sovereign spreads, financing costs and the price of dollar-denominated imports.

The current French episode may stop short of that more damaging scenario. Morgan Stanley’s Kandhari sees France’s fiscal turmoil as a repricing rather than another euro-zone crisis. The country’s fiscal problems are well understood and the European Central Bank now has significantly stronger tools to manage contagion, she said.

The overall setup could leave European equities in something of a sweet spot: enough currency weakness to create upside earnings surprises, without overwhelming the domestic forces supporting the broader market. The result could be a foreign exchange boost that reaches well beyond the exporters benefiting from it directly.

title: Nvidia-backed firm launches US$3.1 bil GPU loan in market
article:
(Oct 28): Zankore, an Indonesian artificial intelligence infrastructure platform backed by Nvidia Corp, is syndicating a US$3.1 billion loan to the broader market, according to people familiar with the matter, adding to a flurry of financing for Asia’s AI buildout.

The five-year loan, which funds the purchase of graphics processing units for Zankore’s new AI factory, will pay an interest margin of 330 basis points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate, said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private matters. United Overseas Bank Ltd and Citigroup Inc are among the five original underwriters marketing the deal, with other banks invited to join in the senior phase as underwriters or bookrunners, the people said.

Citigroup and UOB declined to comment while Zankore did not respond to requests for comment.

The deal adds to a wave of debt financing backing Asia’s AI infrastructure boom, as regional lenders increasingly look beyond data centre construction to financing GPUs. Moody’s Ratings expects at least US$3 trillion in data centre-related investment over the next five years, even as investors scrutinise lofty AI valuations.

Blackstone-owned AirTrunk secured a A$4.25 billion green loan for a Sydney data centre campus while Blue Owl Capital-owned Stack Infrastructure Inc is seeking a A$8.6 billion facility for a buildout in Melbourne.

Zankore’s financing is supported by a six-year contract with Nvidia that includes revenue sharing and credit support, helping reduce lenders’ repayment risk, the people said. The arrangement applies to any unsold compute capacity from an initial 100MW, they said.

See also: Musk says ASML, others expediting chipmaking gear for Terafab

US fintech companies are the offtakers, buying GPU compute capacity from Zankore, the people added.

title: Copper wavers near two-week high as traders look to Fed meeting
article:
(Oct 28): Copper traded near its highest close in two weeks as traders braced for the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates.

The metal slipped 0.2% to US$14,447.50 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange at 1.25pm in Shanghai (same time as Malaysia). Prices climbed more than 1% on Tuesday amid a broader surge for metals fuelled by renewed positive sentiment on artificial intelligence, as well as signs of supply pressure.

At the Fed’s policy meeting later on Wednesday (Oct 28), the focus will be on what the US central bank says about the outlook for the economy and inflation. Officials are seen likely to leave rates unchanged at this gathering but a hike in December is being priced in. Higher borrowing costs can be a headwind for metals.

Copper has gained about 16% this year in a rally powered by supply tightness as huge tonnages were shipped to the US in anticipation of import tariffs. On Wednesday, a key spread on the LME spiked higher, indicating more short-term supply stress.

“As the year-end approaches, US tariff policies on refined copper could generate significant market volatility, with the eventual implementation of these policies likely to drive price trends,” Chinese brokerage Chaos Ternary Futures Co wrote in a note.

Other metals were mixed, with aluminium gaining 0.4% and zinc and nickel little changed.

See also: Iron ore declines to two-year low as demand outlook weakens

title: StanChart beats estimates, raises targets on wealth boom
article:
(Oct 28): Standard Chartered plc posted profit that beat analyst estimates in the third quarter and raised its outlook for income growth and returns.

The London-headquartered bank reported pretax profit of US$2.25 billion ($2.88 billion), surpassing the US$2.09 billion Bloomberg-compiled average analyst estimate. The performance was driven by a strong performance in its global trading business and wealth unit.

“The consistency and breadth of our performance reflects the strength of our franchise and disciplined execution across the group,” chief executive officer Bill Winters said in a statement. “This gives us confidence to raise our 2026 income guidance.”

Alongside its main rival HSBC Holdings plc, Standard Chartered has focused on building its wealth management arm in recent years, looking to manage a greater share of money from Asia’s swelling ranks of mass affluent.

Standard Chartered shares hit an all-time high in September as investors have become more optimistic on the outlook for the bank, but have softened since then amid concerns about a new UK bank tax as well as growing geopolitical tensions.

title: Marcos pledges to ‘do all we can’ to defend Philippine peso
article:
(Oct 28): Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr pledged that Philippine authorities will do all they can to defend the peso as the currency weakened to a record low this week.

“We will continue to do all that we can to make sure that the value of the peso does not continue to go down,” Marcos told reporters in Manila on Wednesday, a day after meeting with central bank and key government officials.

“People can take solace in the fact that our policy toward the peso is to continue to defend the peso as hard as we possibly can,” he said.

Elevated oil prices are deepening losses across most emerging Asian currencies as nations like the Philippines face soaring import costs. The Philippine peso slid more than 8% this year, the biggest loser in Asia.

“Don’t panic,” Marcos urged Filipinos. “It is an effect of rising prices of oil and, consequently, the rising prices of fuel and its effect on the economy.”

See also: Weaker euro boosts European exporters as earnings season peaks

Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas has repeatedly said it does not target a specific exchange level and that it intervenes to smoothen volatility. Philippine foreign-exchange reserves fell to US$100 billion in September, the lowest level in three years.

The peso, which fell to a record low of 64.20 per dollar on Tuesday, is trading at 63.99 on Wednesday.

title: RegCo issues additional queries to SGX-listed companies with links to haze
article:
The Singapore Exchange Regulation (SGX RegCo) says it has issued additional queries to Singapore-listed companies with agricultural operations and plantations in Indonesia on their response to the transboundary haze from Indonesia. The follow-up queries come just a week after companies had responded to SGX RegCo’s earlier queries on their links to the haze.

Earlier, Singapore-listed companies with plantation operations in Indonesia had received queries from SGX RegCo on Oct 15. Specifically, companies were asked about the impact of Indonesia’s forest fires on their operations, how their activities may have contributed to the haze and what they are doing in response to it. The queried companies include: Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Golden Agri-Resources, Indofood Agri Resources, Kencana Agri and Wilmar International.

Companies such as Bumitama Agri, First Resources and Kencana Agri have since responded to SGX RegCo’s queries where they have expressed their willingness to cooperate with investigations. The companies also emphasised their commitment to their zero burning policies.

A spokesperson for SGX RegCo says the additional queries will ensure that all stakeholders can better assess the basis for the disclosures they have made so far as well as the extent of the impact these issuers face.

To that end, SGX RegCo is asking issuers to made disclosures on four key areas.

Firstly, issuers are to disclose the policies and measures they have put in place to monitor, prevent and respond to the fires. They will also have to reveal the bases that support their assessment on the adequacy and effectiveness of such policies and measures.

See also: Singapore expands haze inquiries to 10 locally based firms

Secondly, issuers will have to disclose any links they might have with the 10 Indonesian companies that were issued legal notices under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.

Thirdly, issuers are to disclose their board’s assessment of and the basis for whether the fires and haze have a material impact on the company.

Finally, issuers will have to disclosure any queries or investigations by authorities or agencies in Singapore, Indonesia or elsewhere.

See also: Singapore issues haze notices to three more Indonesian firms

On Oct 27, Singapore and Indonesia announced that the two countries will be establishing a joint task force to investigate companies linked to the forest fires behind the haze.

Minister for Foreign Affairs Dr Vivian Balakrishnan said during a joint press conference with his Indonesian counterpart, Arrmanatha Nasir that Singapore had agreed with Indonesia’s proposal to work together to hold the companies responsible for the haze.

“Singapore agrees, and we are in effect putting all the companies on notice that the joint task force will ensure that there is a very close coordination of actions and sharing of information between Indonesia and Singapore, and we expect, therefore, the deterrent impact of this joint task force to make a difference,” Balakrishnan said.

title: South Korea's financial firms hit by more hacks as Asia breaches grow
article:
(Oct 28): South Korea’s financial industry was hit by a second wave of cyberattacks in about a month as a wave of breaches across Asia heightens concerns that artificial intelligence (AI) is making large-scale hacking easier.

Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin said Wednesday that some of South Korea’s major financial investment companies had suffered widespread hacking the previous day. He urged the industry to strengthen security, without identifying the affected companies.

Institutions including Mirae Asset Global Investments Co and Daishin Securities Co reported unauthorised access, renewing concerns over the vulnerability of the country’s financial system.

South Korea’s Presidential Blue House will hold an emergency meeting to discuss the hack, Yonhap News reported. The Blue House did not offer an immediate comment.

The breaches add to a string of attacks on Japanese companies, including SoftBank Corp and Daiwa Securities Group Inc, that have prompted authorities there to call for security checks. Japan’s Financial Services Agency called for scrutiny of third-party risks and extra precautions when verifying users’ identities online while Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama urged financial institutions to review their defenses.

Earlier this month, attackers using a sophisticated AI agent targeted some of South Korea’s biggest banks and financial institutions.

See also: Thailand holds key rate, lifts growth outlook on AI exports

Organisations worldwide are also working to patch critical flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language widely used across the internet, amid disruptions that have prompted banks, airlines and governments to take websites offline.

Daishin Securities said personal and credit information belonging to 38,490 customers was leaked. Mirae Asset Global, which had US$461 billion ($591 billion) in assets under management at the end of September, reported unauthorised access to some of its business-use web systems.

Daishin said it detected suspicious access on Oct 17 to a server supporting remote account openings. An investigation found that exposed information included customer names, email and physical addresses, and encrypted account and mobile phone numbers. The brokerage said it found no evidence of subsequent harm to customers or unauthorised access to its core business systems.

See also: StanChart beats estimates, raises targets on wealth boom

Mirae Asset said retail investor information wasn’t involved because the affected systems don’t serve those customers. There were no financial losses and its main systems and servers were operating normally, the company said in a statement.

Cryptocurrency exchange Bithumb Co also detected unauthorised access to its internal mobile groupware system Tuesday, according to Yonhap. It is investigating the extent of any data leak, including whether customer information was exposed, the report said. An email seeking comment wasn’t immediately answered.

title: Prabowo to meet Singapore envoy on mission to ease relations
article:
(Oct 28): Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto will meet Singapore’s top diplomat on Wednesday as ties between the two Southeast Asian nations come under strain.

Singapore’s Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan arrived in Indonesia “unexpectedly” on Tuesday morning and requested a meeting with Prabowo, Cabinet Secretary Teddy Indra Wijaya said in a statement. “He will be received briefly later today.”

Prabowo continues to maintain good relations and is strengthening communication with friendly nations, particularly those in Southeast Asia, Wijaya said.

Balakrishnan’s visit is at a sensitive juncture. Haze from wildfires burning in Indonesia blanketed Singapore in smog while Indonesia unexpectedly cut gas supplies to Singapore. A former Indonesian minister also publicly accused Singapore state investment funds of instigating a recent market rout.

On Tuesday, Balakrishnan and his Indonesian counterpart Arrmanatha Nasir said both countries agreed to form a joint taskforce to help tackle the forest fires.

title: Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after fleeing Brazil — O Globo
article:
(Oct 28): Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami on Tuesday after fleeing his country following a defeat in its presidential election, O Globo reported.

Bolsonaro was greeted by his brother Eduardo upon arrival, the newspaper said, citing allies. Eduardo has lived in the US since last year after moving there to lobby US President Donald Trump to help their father, former Brazil president Jair Bolsonaro, who was convicted of plotting a coup.

A senior US State Department official said earlier Tuesday that the US would grant visas to Flávio and his family.

Flávio Bolsonaro, who is facing multiple criminal investigations in Brazil, was ordered to surrender his passports to the Federal Police by Tuesday but failed to do so, according to a police official familiar with the situation. Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, whom the Bolsonaro family has long accused of political persecution, demanded he turn over the documents amid concerns the senator posed a flight risk.

Bolsonaro’s loss to Brazil President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s runoff election dealt a massive setback to a family that had sought to cement a political dynasty in Brazil. The senator had made freeing his father Jair Bolsonaro who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss, a central theme of his campaign.

Trump told reporters early Wednesday after returning from a campaign trip to Texas that he would have approved of Bolsonaro coming to the US but thought that he was in Argentina.

See also: Prabowo to meet Singapore envoy on mission to ease relations

Speaking in Texas on Tuesday afternoon, Trump avoided mentioning Bolsonaro but reiterated his unfounded assertions that there was fraud in Brazil’s election. He assailed Democrats as the “greatest cheaters of elections” before adding that “Brazil’s doing a pretty good job also”.

The US leader has long been an ally of the Bolsonaros and last year placed tariffs on Brazilian goods in an unsuccessful bid to help Jair Bolsonaro avoid his coup trial.

Flávio Bolsonaro’s whereabouts were unknown to police or allies on Tuesday morning after Infobae reported that he had crossed into Argentina and planned to travel to the US from there. Brazil police have no official record of Bolsonaro leaving Brazil, and the press secretary for Argentina President Javier Milei denied that he had entered the country.

See also: Trump and Xi’s managed, competitive coexistence

Multiple Bolsonaro allies told Bloomberg News that they tried to contact him but had not heard back.

The saga has set social media alight with memes referring to Bolsonaro as "Flyvio", comparing him to Carmen Sandiego or Where’s Waldo? Others have altered the conservative slogan, “God, Country and Family” to “Goodbye, Country and Family".

“The act of leaving Brazil is shameful,” Lula said at an event to mark his 81st birthday. The leftist has had a rocky relationship with Trump and earlier this year denied visas to two senior US officials amid fears they planned to question the integrity of its electoral system.

Bolsonaro is facing at least two federal investigations into allegations of money laundering, one of which stems from his links to the former Banco Master SA owner caught in Brazil’s biggest-ever bank fraud case. He has denied wrongdoing.

His actions since the Sunday vote had evoked those of his father even before the reports he was leaving Brazil. He initially said he would request the annulment of the results due to a Supreme Court decision to extend voting hours, echoing Jair Bolsonaro’s refusal to accept his narrow loss to Lula four years ago.

Jair Bolsonaro left Brazil for the US after the defeat. He returned months later and was subsequently barred from holding public office for eight years for spreading false claims about Brazil’s electronic voting system ahead of the election, then convicted of plotting a coup.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Flávio Bolsonaro backed down on his plans to seek annulment of the results Monday, publishing a social media video in which he said the Supreme Court had barred him from leaving Brazil. He said the move followed comments by his brother Eduardo, who said on a podcast that Flávio should leave Brazil if he lost the election.

Moraes’ decision irritated officials in Lula’s government as well as some members of the Supreme Court, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing private conversations.

Lula’s administration had wanted to focus on efforts to pacify the country and move past the polarisation that has exploded during back-to-back election battles between the leftist leader and a member of the Bolsonaro family, the people said. It viewed the move from Moraes, a controversial judge who oversaw Jair Bolsonaro’s trial and has long drawn charges of censorship from the Brazilian right, as counter to those aims.

Earlier Tuesday, Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered federal authorities to open an investigation into possible illegal foreign financing of Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, including by a group linked to US Vice President J D Vance.

The justice stressed that the order does not establish that illegal foreign financing occurred but said allegations levelled during Brazil’s presidential race warrant an investigation. Vance’s office did not respond to a request for comment.

Argentina’s spokesman, Adrian Ravier, said there had been no request for asylum in Argentina from Bolsonaro during a press conference Tuesday.

title: Dongshan precision slips in debut after US$1.3 bil HK listing
article:
(Oct 28): Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co shares slumped on their first day of trading in Hong Kong after the company raised HK$9.9 billion (US$1.3 billion or $1.6 billion), a debut that tests investor appetite for artificial intelligence (AI)-linked listings after a sharp market pullback.

The printed circuit board maker’s stock declined as much as 6.1% early Wednesday, after the company priced 113.8 million shares at HK$86.80 apiece, below the maximum and at a 35% discount to the previous close of its Shenzhen-listed stock. The deal was about half the size of the US$3 billion ($3.9 billion) Dongshan first sought and gave Dongshan Precision a market value of about US$30 billion.

The debut arrives at a tricky moment for Hong Kong. A listing boom has put the 2021 record in share-sale proceeds within reach, but rising bond yields and poor deal performance have made investors and issuers turn more cautious recently. A string of initial public offering withdrawals and delays, including by major data centre operators in the region, has also added pressure that’s prompted some companies in Hong Kong to put near-term listing plans on hold.

“It still looks more like a falling knife, particularly as investors reassess AI-related valuations and spending,” said Gerald Gan, chief investment officer at Singapore-based Reed Capital. The decision to cut the Hong Kong offering from as much as US$3 billion “also tells me that appetite for large deals is becoming more selective — Hong Kong’s IPO pipeline remains active, but investors are increasingly demanding better valuations rather than buying every AI-related listing indiscriminately”.

Dongshan’s was the 10th Hong Kong listing this year to top US$1 billion in proceeds, out of almost 120 deals so far, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The biggest were Zhongji Innolight Co and Luxshare Precision Industry Co, which raised US$7.8 billion and US$3.2 billion, respectively. That’s the most billion-dollar listings since 2020, when there were 16.

See also: Anthropic IPO filing calms nerves with signs of healthy growth

The blowout year has been driven in large part by Chinese companies along the AI supply chain. Other PCB makers with recent listings include Victory Giant Technology Huizhou Co, which raised US$3 billion in one of Hong Kong’s biggest deals of the year, and Shenzhen Kinwong Electronic Co, which completed a US$650 million debut in September.

Cornerstone investors — which get guaranteed allocation in the deal in exchange for holding the stock for at least six months — including JPMorgan Asset Management, Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, CPE and Montage Technology Co, agreed to buy a combined 50% of the offering. Jane Street Group and Jump Trading LLC are also among them.

The Suzhou-based company makes PCBs and optical transceivers, key components for AI. It’s the third-largest PCB supplier in an US$85.2 billion global market, according to its filing.

See also: Acts of God meet acts of AI in private equity’s new debt play

UBS Group AG, Guotai Haitong Securities Co, GF Securities Co and Citic Securities Co are joint sponsors for the Hong Kong listing, according to the preliminary prospectus.

title: Chinese EV imports surge in Thailand ahead of planned excise tax
article:
(Oct 28): Thailand’s imports of electric passenger cars more than doubled in September, almost entirely driven by China, as booming demand and the prospect of higher taxes on fully imported EVs lifted shipments.

Imports surged 138% from a year earlier to US$421 million, with China supplying almost 99% of the total, government data showed. The value was also 86% higher than in August. In the first nine months of the year, Thailand imported US$2.37 billion of electric passenger cars, 96% of them from China.

The surge highlights the challenge Thailand is trying to address with higher taxes on imported EVs. After decades building Southeast Asia’s biggest auto-manufacturing hub, the government wants booming electric-car demand to translate into local production and jobs rather than a growing dependence on vehicles shipped from China.

Thailand is now considering an excise tax of around 30% on fully imported EVs as part of a new structure designed to favor domestic manufacturing. Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas has said the government is working with automakers to finalise the rate.

A three-tier structure approved in principle by Thailand’s EV policy board in September would impose the highest excise tax on fully imported vehicles, a lower rate on cars assembled locally with imported components and the lowest on EVs with greater domestic production and content.

See also: Adani flagship returns to profit as newer businesses deliver

The prospect of higher taxes may already be pulling some imports forward. Nantapong Chiralerspong, director-general of the Trade Policy and Strategy Office, said September’s surge reflected both strong demand and the expansion of Chinese EV brands, with anticipation of the proposed tax potentially accelerating shipments.

The surge comes alongside rapid growth in the domestic EV market. Sales of battery-electric passenger cars jumped 80% from a year earlier to 16,404 in September and nearly doubled to 161,532 in the first nine months, according to the Federation of Thai Industries.

The industry expects that momentum to continue. New EV registrations are forecast to reach 200,000 to 220,000 this year, up from about 120,000 in 2025, according to Surapong Paisitpatnapong, an adviser to the Federation of Thai Industries chairman and spokesman for its Automotive Industry Club. Registrations had already reached 165,040 through September.

title: Oil jumps with Israeli election and Iran attack report in focus
article:
(Oct 28): Oil rose as traders tracked a tight Israeli election, and the Wall Street Journal reported the US has told several Persian Gulf nations to be prepared for a fresh military campaign against Iran after the midterms.

Brent climbed towards US$116 a barrel, snapping a two-day drop, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) was above US$101. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc was tied with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s, according to two exit polls, with both contenders short of the majority needed to become the next leader.

On Iran, the US communications are among a growing number of indications that America and Israel are set to launch a new round of heavy combat operations, according to the Wall Street Journal report, which cited unnamed people briefed on the conversations. US President Donald Trump hasn’t decided to go ahead, but was leaning toward a large post-election attack, it added.

Global crude benchmark Brent has surged by almost 90% this year as the conflict — which began in February when Trump and Netanyahu ordered the initial attack on Tehran — roiled energy flows. Following the Israeli election, American voters will go to the polls Nov 3 for the midterm elections, potentially revealing a slump in support for the administration.

Trump has hinted US strikes against the Islamic Republic could be resumed, and he has sent additional forces, including a third aircraft carrier group, toward the Persian Gulf. At the weekend, the US leader told Fox News that it’s “getting to be decision time” on whether there’ll be a deal or renewed assault.

During the Israeli campaign, Eisenkot pitched himself as a more modest alternative to Netanyahu, while still emphasising a push to resolving security challenges. On Iran, he said the country’s nuclear programme must be curbed, militarily if necessary, but regime change is “not an achievable goal”.

See also: Aramco contains fire near Ras Tanura oil hub after attack — Bloomberg

There is “a very real possibility President Trump loses his willing war-in-Iran partner, Benjamin Netanyahu”, said Robert Yawger, director of the energy futures division at Mizuho Securities USA LLC. “The vote in Israel could be seen as a preview of what to expect in the US midterm elections.”
• Brent for December settlement advanced 1.4% to US$115.47 a barrel at 9.49am in Singapore.

See also: Oil declines as Iran diplomacy picks up before Israeli, US votes

In the Middle East, risks remain elevated as Saudi energy infrastructure has faced repeated attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels. The latest incident sparked a fire near the kingdom’s biggest oil export terminal at Ras Tanura early Tuesday. While it was contained, according to a person familiar with the matter, the extent of any damage wasn’t immediately clear.

Meanwhile, Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority threatened to take legal action against vessels owned by Sinokor, citing repeated so-called violations over the past three months. The world’s biggest oil tanker owner has carried millions of barrels out of Strait of Hormuz in recent weeks.

On the physical front, the industry-funded American Petroleum Institute reported US crude stockpiles fell by two million barrels last week, according to a document seen by Bloomberg. Official data are due later on Wednesday.

Traders are also set to track the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision in the session. Policymakers are expected to keep borrowing costs steady.

title: Asian stocks rise, Treasuries steady before Fed decision
article:
(Oct 28): Asian stocks climbed for a second consecutive day as enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence trade (AI) lifted equities ahead of earnings from tech megacaps and the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest-rate decision.

The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.8%, led by a 4.5% jump in South Korea’s Kospi Index. That came after SK Hynix Inc’s stock climbed following a stronger-than-expected sevenfold surge in profit. The chipmaker is planning a total of 100 trillion won (US$75 billion or $96 billion) in shareholder returns for 2026.

The optimistic tone came as Alphabet Inc and Microsoft Corp prepared to report earnings Wednesday, while Amazon.com Inc is set to announce on Thursday.

Elsewhere, global crude oil benchmark Brent pared some of its losses from the previous two sessions as traders assessed efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Persian Gulf. The commodity rose 0.4% to around US$114.35 a barrel. Treasuries were little changed, while the dollar held its gains from the previous two sessions.

Optimism around the AI trade rebounded this week after a recent rout in chip stocks, but it faces a key test from megacap tech earnings in the next few days. Investors are also awaiting the Fed’s rate decision for clues on the policy outlook as elevated bond yields and persistent inflation complicate the case for lower borrowing costs.

“A wave of AI news sparked a relief rally after three weeks of pressure on the group,” Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading Institutional Services LLC, wrote in a note. That news has “offered solace to investors that the large-scale AI firms can, and are proceeding to spend even if smaller firms are under pressure”.

See also: Tech rally extends to Asia on Anthropic, oil falls

In geopolitical news, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot are neck and neck in the first election since the 2023 Hamas attacks, setting up a tense period of negotiations over who will form the next government.

Elsewhere, gold held its gains from the previous session, when bullion jumped 1.1% to about US$4,060 an ounce.

On Tuesday, a US gauge of chipmakers jumped 3.6%, sending Wall Street benchmarks higher. Meta Platforms Inc’s US$25 billion share sale was five times oversubscribed, while Oracle Corp expanded its partnership with OpenAI.

See also: Mercuria says rival fears drove disputed Baltic tanker rate

The main focus on Wednesday will be the Fed decision. The Fed will be followed by rate decisions from the European Central Bank and Bank of Japan this week.

The Fed is expected to keep rates steady, even after inflation data for September came in hotter than expected.

If they do stay put, chairman Kevin Warsh could face pressure to explain policymakers’ rationale for not acting now after they voted unanimously last month to raise rates to address burgeoning inflation.

On Tuesday, data showed US consumer confidence unexpectedly rose in October for the first time in four months, buoyed by brighter views on the labour market and business conditions. The reading topped all forecasts in a Bloomberg survey of economists.

The “moderate rebound in US consumer sentiment and decline in oil prices seem to have supported risk sentiment going into a busy week of central bank decisions”, said Dan Pan, an Americas economist at Standard Chartered Bank. “A hawkish hold seems to be the baseline but we would argue that the market might be underestimating the risks for a hike.”
• Jio Platforms Ltd’s US$3.1 billion India-record initial public offering has attracted stellar demand across investor categories ahead of its Oct 28 market debut.
• Solidigm Inc, an American subsidiary of the South Korean memory-chip maker SK Hynix Inc, is in talks with the US Commerce Department to invest US$45 billion in a new US chip plant, according to people familiar with the negotiations.
• Banks are planning to sell as much as about US$21 billion of high-grade bonds as soon as early next year as part of a US$63 billion funding package that Broadcom Inc has pulled together to help finance chips for AI developer Anthropic.

title: Anthropic said to pick JPMorgan to lead IPO’s US retail offering — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 28): Anthropic PBC has tapped JPMorgan Chase & Co to lead US sales of shares to individual investors in its potentially record-setting initial public offering, people familiar with the matter said.

The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall, some of the people said. JPMorgan chief executive officer Jamie Dimon is expected to take part in the Wall Street bank’s campaign, one of them added.

JPMorgan is reprising its role leading the effort to gather retail orders for SpaceX’s US$86.2 billion IPO, which saw more than US$100 billion of demand from individual investors, Bloomberg News has reported.

Citigroup Inc. is set to coordinate the international retail offering, some of the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Anthropic’s IPO includes offerings in Australia, Canada, Japan, certain European Economic Area countries, Switzerland and the UK, according to the IPO filing.

JPMorgan is coordinating outreach on Anthropic’s IPO to high-net-worth investors and private banking clients, as well as broker platforms, the people said.

Deliberations are ongoing and details including the share of the offering earmarked for retail could change, the people said. Representatives for Anthropic, JPMorgan and Citigroup declined to comment.

Anthropic filed publicly on Monday for an IPO that would see it and some of its investors sell shares, marking the first listing by a company focused primarily on developing the most advanced AI models. Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering.

Investors are telling bankers on the deal that their estimate of a fair valuation has shifted to around US$1.4 trillion to US$1.5 trillion, though a valuation of closer to US$1.75 trillion is potentially achievable, Bloomberg News has reported.

The amount of money needed to fund the development of AI and its associated infrastructure has spurred companies to raise tens of billions of dollars at a time.

See also: Dubai firm’s US$543 mil IPO covered within minutes despite war

Meta Platforms Inc on Monday kicked off a plan to raise as much as US$98 billion in equity, which would be one of the largest financing exercises of its kind in history. It follows Google parent Alphabet Inc’s US$85 billion equity fundraising plan earlier this year.

Anthropic and rival OpenAI are seeking to raise record amounts while facing mounting public scrutiny over AI safety after a string of high-profile hacking incidents by rogue agents.

title: Seatrium and Karpowership explore JV for floating power solutions in Singapore
article:
Mainboard-listed Seatrium has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Turkish energy company Karpowership to pursue a joint venture to develop floating power and infrastructure solutions in Singapore.

The partnership was announced at Singapore International Energy Week on Oct 27 and was witnessed by Tan See Leng, Singapore’s Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry).

Under the MoU, the two companies plan to create an integrated platform combining infrastructure development, financing, engineering, construction and operations. It also establishes a framework to jointly develop rapidly deployable power and infrastructure solutions in Singapore, which may include Powerships, floating data centres, turbine-based or hybrid vessels and floating nuclear solutions.

Across Southeast Asia, the similar growth of digital industries has also led to increased infrastructure requirements. According to the 9th ASEAN Energy Outlook, 20% of ASEAN's projected electricity demand growth in the next five years will be attributable to data centres. Coupled with structural drivers of industrialisation and urbanisation, generation capacity for reliable power to support industrial activity and other energy-intensive facilities is crucial.

Against this backdrop, floating power infrastructure could provide additional options to enhance supply security, including through the rapid deployment of generation capacity, contingency power provision and support for critical infrastructure, including data centres. Such solutions could also offer flexibility in deployment locations, enable power generation assets to be adapted or redeployed, and chart a longer-term transition pathway as energy requirements continue to evolve.

Seatrium CEO Chris Ong says that Seatrium’s offshore engineering heritage, systems integration capabilities and advanced facilities in Singapore provide a strong foundation to strengthen Singapore’s status as a hub for next-generation floating energy and digital infrastructure, supporting domestic needs and opportunities across the region.

See also: Singapore’s EMA backs grid resilience projects with $14.9 mil

“As demand for power and digital infrastructure accelerates, our industry has an opportunity to develop new solutions that combine speed of deployment, flexibility and scale,”remarks Ong. “For Seatrium, this represents a strategic opportunity to extend our role across the energy infrastructure value chain, creating new avenues for growth where we can apply our proven capabilities to shape critical infrastructure that underpin the region’s future competitiveness.”

Karpowership CEO Orhan Remzi Karadeniz says that the firm’s decades-long relationships with OEMs and technology partners, including Seatrium and hyperscalers, position Karpowership as a go-to provider of integrated infrastructure solutions at pace and scale.

“Together with Seatrium, our ambition is to build an integrated platform in Singapore that brings development, financing, engineering and operations together to deliver power where and when it is needed, strengthening energy security and enabling growth across Southeast Asia,” says Karadeniz.

title: DBS sees nuclear opportunities
article:
To seize money-making opportunities in financing nuclear energy projects presumably, banks have to build up the capability and knowledge in the subject to be part of the nuclear power ecosystem, suggests Ganesh Padmanabhan, managing director and head of project finance at DBS, Singapore’s largest and most profitable bank.

Speaking at a Singapore International Energy Week panel on Oct 27, Padmanabhan shares that due to various reasons including regulations and project size and scale, nuclear power is “beyond the reach” of commercial bank funding. “From a financing standpoint, historically, nuclear hasn't had commercial bank financing at all,” he says. “There's no track record.”

Because commercial banks have not had a need to consider nuclear opportunities, they have not developed the expertise to evaluate such projects. However, with the emergence of small modular reactors (SMRs) which are smaller and less costly, banks may have the opportunity to finance nuclear power, mentions Padmanabhan.

“I think the banks also have to build that capability and that knowledge to be able to walk alongside the developers, the regulators, and other stakeholders in this area,” says Padmanabhan. Presumably, with expertise in nuclear, banks would be able to evaluate risks and opportunities in nuclear power projects.

He also suggests other considerations including risk diversification among stakeholders. “So to me, I think covering risk elements through support from the government, be it in the form of some kind of a regulatory asset, a PPP [public-private partnership] model, or even bringing an export credit agency into supporting these, will make it a bit more bankable to bring in commercial banks into the financing mix itself,” remarks Padmanabhan.

While Singapore has not yet made a decision on adopting nuclear energy, it is aggressively preparing itself for such a possibility with a raft of initiatives in recent months. These include announcing talent development programmes in nuclear and collaborations with other countries on knowledge sharing and research.

On the commercial front, Mainboard-listed Sembcorp Industries and ST Engineering will be collaborating to prepare themselves for nuclear energy. Sembcorp will also partner Canadian nuclear engineering firm AtkinsRéalis to “explore collaboration opportunities” in the nuclear energy sector.

Overall, Singapore is building capabilities across 19 key areas identified by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) as necessary for a country to establish a nuclear power programme. Areas include funding and financing, industrial involvement, nuclear safety and radioactive waste management, among others.

Furthermore, to assess its readiness and ensure these capability building efforts are advancing in the right direction, Singapore has embarked on the Integrated Nuclear Infrastructure Review (INIR) conducted by the IAEA.

Speaking at the same panel, Kim Han Gon, president of the Innovative Small Modular Reactor (i-SMR) Development Agency, says that financial risk associated with a first-of-its-kind project is a hurdle hindering SMR commercialisation. “This [financial] risk is particularly significant when the full project relies on private investment, so our approach is to reduce this financial risk step by step,” he adds.

The i-SMR Development Agency is a South Korean government-backed organisation established to lead the development and commercialisation of the country's homegrown i-SMR.

With government backing and collaborations with Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power (KHNP) and Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), Kim says the agency aims to de-risk first deployment. He expects that a successful i-SMR project will provide reference design and clear evidence on the construction costs, schedule, and performance. “This experience will make subsequent projects easier for private investment,” he states.

He sees opportunities for different forms of private participation at different stages. “Industrial partners may participate in the projects, because of their technical capability and their long-term business interests [while] broader private investment can then expand as the technology and delivery model becomes more established,” he says. “Our goal is to reduce the risk, but it does not mean that we can guarantee that investors will never lose money.”

Shares in DBS closed at $73.92 on Oct 27. Ytd, the counter is up by more than 30%.

title: US stocks rise in run-up to tech results as oil falls
article:
(Oct 28): A rally in technology companies lifted stocks ahead of this week’s results from industry giants valued at more than US$10 trillion, with traders also bracing for the Federal Reserve rate decision.

Renewed enthusiasm around artificial intelligence drove a closely watched gauge of chipmakers up 3.6%. The Nasdaq 100 added 1.3%. Meta Platforms Inc’s US$25 billion share sale ended five times oversubscribed. Oracle Corp is expanding a partnership with OpenAI. United Parcel Service Inc climbed on a solid outlook. Boeing Co sank 11% after cutting its delivery target.

In a volatile session, Brent oil settled below US$114 as traders weighed moves to de-escalate tensions in the Persian Gulf. Bonds barely budged. The dollar rose.

Three of the world’s biggest companies — Alphabet Inc, Microsoft Corp and Amazon.com Inc — are expected to show healthy growth when they report earnings this week. But for Wall Street, what matters is: How much they’re spending on AI and when the investment will pay off in a meaningful way.

Not all big techs should be treated equally regarding potential growth, according to Chris Brigati at SWBC.

“The period of a rising market lifting all stocks has started to shift,” he said. “Future expectations are more focused upon execution risk and how much future success is already embedded in the current stock price.”

See also: Tech stocks power Wall Street gains as oil falls

Meantime, US policymakers will likely keep rates steady on Wednesday, opting to bide their time before potential further increases.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who’s eschewed guidance on future moves, will face a tricky test at his post-meeting conference. He probably won’t offer much insight about December, but may also not want to sway market bets away from the current expectation for a hike.

All in all, economic data suggest there’s no good reason to delay tightening, according to Jerry Tempelman at Mutual of America Capital Management. But by having signaled it intends to wait until December, the Fed has now more or less “boxed itself in,” he added. That means it would surprise markets if it were to lift rates on Wednesday.

See also: Whirlpool cuts outlook again on lacklustre demand, soaring costs

“We think an increase at the end of the year is likely, with one further rate hike anticipated for 2027, as the central bank looks to combat inflation and lean against any acceleration in growth,” said James McCann at Edward Jones.

title: Tech stocks power Wall Street gains as oil falls
article:
(Oct 27): A rally in technology companies lifted stocks ahead of results from industry giants valued at more than US$10 trillion, with traders also bracing for the Federal Reserve rate decision.

Despite losses in most of its companies, the S&P 500 advanced. A closely watched gauge of chipmakers climbed 2.3%. Meta Platforms Inc’s US$25 billion stock sale was said to have attracted demand for about five times the available shares. Brent crude dropped below US$115. Treasuries wavered.

Investor enthusiasm around artificial intelligence (AI) returned after the trade took a drubbing over the past few weeks amid concerns about the amount of debt fuelling the infrastructure buildout.

Three of the world’s biggest companies — Alphabet Inc, Microsoft Corp and Amazon.com Inc — are expected to show healthy growth when they report earnings this week. But for Wall Street, what really matters these days is: How much money they’re spending on AI and when it will start to pay off in a meaningful way.

“It’s going to be very interesting to see how these stocks react to their earnings/guidance,” said Matt Maley at Miller Tabak. “So far, many tech names have sold off following their reports.

See also: US stocks rise in run-up to tech results as oil falls

Therefore, given how important these companies are to the AI phenomenon, their reactions should be particularly important.”

Meantime, the Fed and its peers in the eurozone and Japan will probably keep interest rates steady this week, opting to bide their time before potential further hikes.

Fed chairman Kevin Warsh, who’s eschewed guidance on future moves, will face a tricky test at his post-meeting press conference Wednesday. He probably won’t offer much insight about December, but may also not want to sway market bets away from the current expectation for a hike.

See also: Whirlpool cuts outlook again on lacklustre demand, soaring costs

On the economic front, US consumer confidence unexpectedly rose in October for the first time in four months as views about the job market and business conditions improved.

Despite the increase in confidence this month, consumers remain troubled by the impact of higher prices on their budgets and on wage growth that is lagging behind inflation. Borrowing costs have also climbed more recently, making homes, vehicles and other big-ticket purchases less affordable.
• Broadcom Inc has arranged a US$63 billion deal with Bank of America Corp, Blackstone Inc, Citigroup Inc and Morgan Stanley to finance the purchase of chips for AI model developer Anthropic PBC.
• United Parcel Service Inc boosted its financial guidance for the year above Wall Street’s estimates, suggesting the courier expects to benefit from high prices and resilient demand through the holiday season.

• JetBlue Airways Corp reassured Wall Street that it’s still on track to be profitable in the near future, despite deepening its projected operating margin loss for the current year as fuel costs soar.
• General Motors Co plans to shift its stock listing to the Nasdaq Global Select Market from its longtime home on the New York Stock Exchange, an attempt to position the old-school automaker as a tech-forward company embracing automated driving and electric vehicles.

title: JetBlue shares soar after it vows to return to profitability
article:
(Oct 28): JetBlue Airways Corp reassured Wall Street that it’ll be profitable next year, as the debt-laden carrier seeks to overcome persistent losses and high oil prices to prevent a deeper restructuring.

Chief executive officer Joanna Geraghty reaffirmed the company’s confidence in achieving operating profitability in 2027 and delivering at least US$1 earnings per share and positive free cash flow in 2028 in its third-quarter (3Q) earnings report.

“Despite significant fuel headwinds and a challenging summer operation, our revenue performance is among the strongest in the industry,” Geraghty told analysts on a conference call on Tuesday. She added that JetBlue has “multiple avenues” to strengthen liquidity to bridge the carrier to 2028, such as aircraft financing.

JetBlue rose 20% to US$2.86 as of 11am New York time, with other US major carriers seeing fractional or single-digit gains. The stock had sunk to its lowest level on record on Monday before the earnings report was released, sliding by as much as 18%.

The results underscore how soaring jet fuel prices are eating into airline profits despite resilient demand for travel. JetBlue’s more profitable rivals — such as Delta Air Lines Inc, American Airlines Group Inc and Southwest Airlines Co — all cut their profit outlooks in recent weeks. That signalled that even carriers better insulated from war-related spikes are being squeezed.

See also: IndiGo, Air India to shift some flights to new Mumbai airport

The future outlook is a rare bright spot for the New York-based carrier this quarter. JetBlue anticipates a negative operating margin of 4.5% to 6.5% for 2026, compared with the average analyst estimates for a loss of 5.8%, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. It had previously guided for an operating margin loss of 2% to 5% for the full year. The metric represents the percentage of revenue left over after paying operating costs.

The company reported an adjusted 3Q loss of 60 cents a share, missing Wall Street estimates for a loss of 55 cents a share.

The report comes at a critical moment for JetBlue, which is saddled with roughly US$9 billion in debt. A group of creditors, including holders of US$2 billion in bonds due 2031 and a US$742 million first-lien loan, was working with restructuring advisers PJT Partners and Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld. Wall Street has been watching JetBlue closely ever since Spirit Airlines shut down earlier this year.

See also: VietJet faces aircraft, cash seizures in FitzWalter debt fight

“Debt investors continue to price in a default on its loyalty-backed debt and its convert,” TD Securities analyst Tom Fitzgerald wrote in an Oct 26 note to clients. “Credit investors expressed concern that incremental financings are akin to ‘robbing Peter to pay Paul.’”

Geraghty told analysts “there’s a significant disconnect” between the narrative in the bond market and what JetBlue’s financial results are demonstrating. The conference call ended abruptly after a technical issue.

JetBlue also faces elevated costs and intense competition. The airline has posted six consecutive years of operating losses. The last profitable year on an operating basis was 2019, when operating income was about US$800 million.

“Guidance is for an inflection in free cash flow at the end of 2027, though the company will need to reduce burn significantly prior to that target,” George Ferguson, a Bloomberg Intelligence senior industry analyst, said in a research note on Monday. “Its outlook for 4Q appears challenging.”
